findings: The 2026-entry Utrecht Language and Culture Studies BA is primarily Dutch-taught and includes English courses. Article 3.5 and Annex 1 require 15 EC thematic orientation, 15 EC in one language/culture/history area, 7.5 EC humanities theory, a 90 EC approved specialization, and an internship or study abroad. The Dutch introductory pair is Literary Analysis and Introduction to Language and Communication. The 90 EC Language and Communication specialization comprises 15 EC disciplinary and methods preparation, the 30 EC Culture, Communication and Diversity core, a 30 EC second package, and 15 EC in thesis preparation and the thesis. The earlier second communication package overlaps the core in several timetabling bands and would leave a clash with the research lab when scheduled wholly in year three. The revised sample uses the formal StagePlus option, with Knowledge for Society, the Audiovisual Media Practicum and an approved 15 EC internship. The practicum is part of the faculty’s humanities practice offering, with collaborative media production, evidence and reflection. Under Article 3.5.5 the StagePlus internship also satisfies the separate practical/international requirement, freeing 7.5 EC for electives. The 127.5 EC selected requirements and 52.5 EC electives total 180. A zero-credit portfolio is compulsory under Article 7.5.

The first-year sample places the two named introductory pairs in blocks 1 and 2, and Methods and Statistics 1 (BC) and Face-to-Face Communication (AD) in block 3. The dated CoursePlanner course and TCS registration guidance establish the block 3 occurrence despite the package summary’s block 2. The four core courses run in blocks 1 through 4 in Year 2. Year 2 electives include suitable prior film study, such as Introduction to Film, to prepare for the audiovisual practicum. The core supplies 30 advanced EC before Year 3 and satisfies the 15 advanced EC prerequisite for Knowledge for Society. The TCS direction and thesis guidance explicitly route core completers into host-programme thesis preparation and the named thesis; the lab catalog uses CIW baseline wording and has a group for this core. For the illustrated TCS pathway the approved preparation and all four core units are completed, applying the TCS-specific direction rules. Year 3 block 1 pairs the humanities theory course (C) with CIW Lab (AD); the thesis follows in block 2, after more than 120 EC, and the StagePlus studies and placement are arranged in Year 3. The practicum occupies block 3 and the approved internship can be scheduled flexibly around classes. Year 1 has 45 named and 15 elective EC, Year 2 has 30 named and 30 elective EC, Year 3 has 52.5 named and 7.5 elective EC. There are 75 advanced EC in the specialization, 7.5 introductory EC there, and at least 90 EC at level 2 or above overall even before counting electives. The future-year sequence is an illustration based on the published 2026 cohort requirements and current course periods.

The closest response uses close reading, art history, film interpretation, historical inquiry and social research to study cultural representation and public life. Research Methods and Statistics strengthens empirical methods alongside Qualitative Research Methodology. Renaissance art and the advanced art-history and historical seminars contribute well-defined inquiry through their official descriptions. The media plan adds programming, text and web data, AI ethics, television and digital representation to documentary work, media archaeology and critical interpretation. These are complementary digital humanities tools rather than a specialist film-production degree. The colonial histories and gender plan uses oral history, postcolonial theory, race and media, Indigenous historical inquiry, gender analysis and social movements. Politics and ethics provide institutional and interpretive context. All three are feasible and distinct; other coherent direction clusters remain at the three-option limit. Six pairings reflect actual shared methods or subject matter. Neither large external package is equated to a single UCR course. Where UCR overlaps through multiple courses or differs in method or scope, rows stay separate. The Utrecht internship and 7.5 EC thesis remain explicit. UCR independent research is an optional comparison element outside the schedule.
